title: Multi-Horizon Future Discovery for Physics-Informed Exploration
abstract: arXiv:2610.35468v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Exploration in physical control environments requires agents to identify actions whose consequences reveal previously unexplored aspects of the underlying dynamics. However, many intrinsic motivation methods rely on immediate prediction errors, state novelty, or local physical changes, which may overlook informative outcomes that emerge across extended temporal horizons. We investigate whether learning structured representations of reachable futures can provide a more effective basis for exploration. To this end, we introduce Hamiltonian Temporal Contrastive Curiosity (HTC$^2$), a framework that combines multi-horizon temporal representation learning with Hamiltonian phase-space structure. A horizon-conditioned contrastive critic learns temporal relationships from future-state pairs sampled within the same episode. translated_title: 面向物理知情探索的多时间跨度未来发现
translated_abstract: 在物理控制环境中进行探索，要求智能体识别那些其后果能够揭示底层动力学中先前未被探索方面的动作。然而，许多内在动机方法依赖于即时预测误差、状态新颖性或局部物理变化，这可能忽略在较长时间跨度上涌现出的信息丰富的结果。我们研究学习可达未来的结构化表示是否能为探索提供更有效的基础。为此，我们提出了哈密顿时间对比好奇心，这是一个将多时间跨度时序表示学习与哈密顿相空间结构相结合的框架。视界条件化的对比评价器从同一回合内采样的未来状态对中学习时间关系。正样本对表示之间的距离随后被用作内在奖励，鼓励智能体探索未来……
tldr: 该论文提出HTC²框架，将多时间跨度的时序表示学习与哈密顿相空间结构相结合，以正样本对表示间的距离作为内在奖励，为物理控制环境中的智能体探索提供了更有效的驱动机制。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces HTC² (Hamiltonian Temporal Contrastive Curiosity), a framework that combines multi-horizon temporal representation learning with Hamiltonian phase-space structure, using the distance between positive-pair representations as intrinsic reward to enable more effective exploration in physical control environments.
